title: Tied candidates: the returned order is not a verdict
notice: Synthetic and illustrative. Card names, facts and identifiers are invented. Arguments follow the server's input schemas; results show only some of the fields the server returns.
demonstrates: Hard constraints are sent as constraints, and nothing is saved without asking.
Each candidate's rank field is the methodology's order, not a quality score.
Candidates that match the goal equally are presented without a winner.
Different reward currencies are not treated as equal money.

steps.text: I want a personal card for dining with no annual fee. What should I get?

Before I use Rewardopedia: it keeps a sanitized history of each Rewardopedia request in your Rewardopedia account until you delete it, and it saves facts you tell me unless you ask me not to. Both are shared across assistants connected to your account, and you can ask what is saved or ask me to forget it at any time. Please don't share card or account numbers. I'll search now without saving your preferences; tell me if you want me to remember them.

Two personal cards with a $0 annual fee fit your dining goal. They match it equally, so neither is ranked above the other; Rewardopedia lists tied cards in a fixed identifier order. Example Bistro Card: 3% cash back on dining up to a quarterly cap whose amount Rewardopedia doesn't have, and a 3% foreign transaction fee. Example Supper Card: 3 Example Points per $1 on dining and no foreign transaction fee. Cash back and points are different currencies, so the two 3s are not the same value. Which matters more to you: simple cash back, or no fee when you spend abroad?
